project_metadata.project_name: AI-Personalized Learning Paths — Lumina Learning Group (Synthetic Org Simulation)
project_metadata.brief_reference: Self-directed portfolio project, not tied to a course brief. Designed to showcase Purdue PG cert skills (DS-ML-DL-NLP completed; GenAI in progress) applied to an L&D problem.
project_metadata.current_status: Phase 1 is complete (NB01 to NB04, Oct 2026). NB04 is read only and produced 4 figures in reports/figures: curation flow (30 matches: 11 auto-approved, 19 L&D reviewed: 12 approved, 4 switched, 2 replaced, 1 content gap KSB018); path phasing (caps 35 course hours and 6 KSBs per cycle; 8 / 22 / 25 employees need 1 / 2 / 3 or more cycles, ADR-0050, ADR-0055); two contrasting paths EMP0476 ID Lead vs EMP0188 Solution Architect with privacy gate (ADR-0052); KPI dashboard (K2.2 and K2.1, actual vs projected vs target, best-case footnote). 55 ADRs. Packaged for GitHub (Oct 2026). Phase 2: GenAI upgrade, coming soon. Phase 3: coming soon.

certification_context.learner_background: L&D professional, 18+ years experience, upskilling in DS/ML/DL/NLP/GenAI (Purdue PG certification program)
certification_context.why_this_project: Demonstrates applied AI/NLP skills within the learner's own domain of expertise (L&D/instructional design), rather than a generic public dataset project. Chosen to complement the NLPCapstone01 (K8 Reviews) capstone with a domain-authentic, self-designed system.
certification_context.learning_goal: Build a full pipeline, from org/strategy/competency modeling through NLP-driven course matching and personalized path generation, designed to extend in later phases without a schema rebuild.

course_sourcing_strategy.primary_dataset: Procedurally generated synthetic course catalog (150 rows) built by a COURSE_SPEC-style generator (ADR-0034), plus 4 real arXiv-abstract rows (CRS151-CRS154) = 154 rows. All 30 KSBs covered by 3-5 courses each; 20 orphan/generic courses.
course_sourcing_strategy.credibility_sample: 4 courses (CRS151-CRS154) using real arXiv abstracts as a separate NLP proof-of-concept, clearly labeled. Abstracts pasted in by the user; the CSV must be saved as UTF-8. No target_ksb_id / target_competency_id.
course_sourcing_strategy.rejected_approach: Direct web scraping of course content — legal/stability risk, replaced by fake repository + manually-collected real excerpts
course_sourcing_strategy.course_source_field: courses.course_source (ADR-0031) simulates a multi-source ingestion layer: Lumina_LMS, KonectIn, Ksera, Hiword, arXiv. Provider mix: Lumina_LMS 91 / KonectIn 23 / Ksera 20 / Hiword 16 / arXiv 4. Shown to the NB03 curation reviewer.
course_sourcing_strategy.catalog_generation_thread4: ADR-0034: courses.csv is built by a COURSE_SPEC-style procedural generator, mirroring the parametric-generation discipline used for employees.csv (ROLE_SPEC).
course_sourcing_strategy.label_columns_thread4: ADR-0038: target_ksb_id and target_competency_id persisted (24 NULL). Benchmarking only; never used as inputs by the matching engines and hidden from the NB03 reviewer.
course_sourcing_strategy.catalog_protection_thread5: ADR-0047: NB01 Cluster 4 save behind REGENERATE_COURSES = False. A deliberate rebuild requires re-pasting the arXiv abstracts and re-running NB02.
course_sourcing_strategy.title_clash_note: Thread 5: template titles mean two different courses can share a title (e.g. CRS083 and CRS089, 'GenAI Tool Fluency for L&D Professionals'). Flagged during curation as a catalog-quality issue.

matching_engine.note: ADR-0035 (kickoff) and Thread 4 results. Built in NB02.
matching_engine.production_method: tfidf — TF-IDF cosine similarity (521-word vocabulary on the full catalog + KSB text)
matching_engine.comparison_method: embedding — Sentence-BERT all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine similarity (384 dimensions)
matching_engine.persistence: BOTH tfidf and embedding rows persisted to course_ksb_mapping (4,620 each, 9,240 total), flagged by is_production (True only for tfidf). is_recommended is flagged separately per method (30 True each).
matching_engine.agreement_result: TF-IDF and embeddings pick the same top course for 17 of 30 KSBs. Average top score 0.669 (TF-IDF) vs 0.690 (embedding). Average score gap 0.090, largest 0.255 (KSB003).
matching_engine.accuracy_result: Using target_ksb_id, the top course for each KSB targets the right KSB for 30/30 under both methods. Disagreements mean two valid candidates, not one method being wrong (ADR-0039). This made the NB03 review a choice among valid courses.
matching_engine.explainability: TF-IDF match_explanation lists the top shared keywords; embedding rows carry a generic semantic-similarity note.
matching_engine.duplicate_detection: Course-to-course cosine similarity on the MiniLM vectors. Threshold 0.95 chosen from the distribution. Connected components give 12 clusters covering 27 courses (courses.likely_duplicate_of, courses.duplicate_cluster_id). Detection only; nothing is removed or merged. NB03 per-path duplicate check needed 0 swaps.

curation_layer.note: ADR-0036 design; ADR-0042 NB02 rule; ADR-0043 NB03 L&D review (resolved).
curation_layer.nb02_rule: For the 30 TF-IDF is_recommended rows: ld_approved if methods agree AND score gap < 0.10, else ld_reviewed. Result 11 ld_approved, 19 ld_reviewed.
curation_layer.nb03_review: Blind side-by-side review sheet (suggested TF-IDF course vs alternative MiniLM course; title, description, course_source, format, duration, ksb_layer, duplicate cluster, score; target labels hidden). Decisions: approve / switch / reject + replacement_course_id / reject with no replacement (content gap). Every reject or switch has a reviewer_note.
curation_layer.status_mapping: approve -> ld_approved; switch or reject-with-replacement -> chosen row ld_modified and algorithm's pick ld_rejected; reject without replacement -> ld_rejected (content gap).
curation_layer.result: 12 approve, 4 switch (KSB010, KSB014, KSB015, KSB029), 2 replace (KSB019 -> CRS085, KSB025 -> CRS114), 1 content gap (KSB018). TF-IDF rows: 23 ld_approved, 6 ld_modified, 7 ld_rejected, 0 ld_reviewed, 4,584 algo_suggested. Embedding rows all algo_suggested. 29 of 30 KSBs have exactly one eligible course.
audit_files: outputs/curation_review_sheet_completed.csv (reviewer decisions, hand-edited, CSV UTF-8, read-only to code)
curation_layer.downstream_rule: Only ld_approved / ld_modified rows are eligible input to learning_path_recommendations.

path_engine.input: employee_ksb_gaps with gap_size > 0 (687 open gaps: 540 x 1, 144 x 2, 3 x 3) + one approved course per KSB.
path_engine.ordering: Courses first, content gaps last; biggest gap first; within a competency Knowledge > Skill > Behavior (ksbs.ksb_type).
path_engine.shared_course: A course serving two KSBs for one employee takes one step (shared sequence_order); rationale says 'Also covers ...'. One row per open gap kept for traceability. 98 rows use a shared course (CRS085, CRS114).
path_engine.duplicate_check: Later near-copy in the same duplicate_cluster_id replaced by the earlier course. 0 swaps needed.
path_engine.ksb_layer_use: Fit check only: mismatch between course ksb_layer and the KSB's ksb_type is noted in the rationale; no reordering or dropping.
path_engine.content_gaps: KSB018 has no approved course; 19 employees get a 'coming soon' step. Message in CONTENT_GAP_MESSAGES: 'New workshop/simulation planned for Q1 2027. Meanwhile, use your manager 1:1s or the mentor-mentee programme to build this skill.'

comparison_benchmarks.note: Comparison/exploratory only (ADR-0023). Not persisted to course_ksb_mapping. Artifacts saved to outputs/.

classifier.model: Logistic Regression on TF-IDF features (vectorizer fit on train only)
classifier.data: 130 labeled courses, stratified 91 train / 39 test, random_state=42
classifier.result: 39/39 correct (100%). TF-IDF scored with full match_score also 39/39.
classifier.limitation: Template-generated text gives each competency its own vocabulary, so the benchmark cannot separate the methods. Real catalogs would score lower.

lda.topic_count_method: Perplexity showed no elbow; coherence (c_v) used instead. After removing 33 filler words, coherence peaked at k=12 (0.689).
lda.result: COMP05 and COMP10 captured cleanly; COMP04, COMP05 and COMP09 share one topic; others spread across 2-3 topics. Roughly recovers competency structure without labels, but not cleanly.
lda.limitation: Competency labels were used to find filler words, so that step is not purely unsupervised.

kpi_impact_rollup.note: ADR-0036 design; ADR-0046 implementation (NB03 Step 3.6). Aggregate only, no new table.
kpi_impact_rollup.home: Computed in NB03; charted in NB04 Step 4.5 (fig_4_5_kpi_dashboard.png).
kpi_impact_rollup.k22_method: Actual: competency gaps that moved from positive (prior_year) to zero or below (current_year), x 3 KSBs, averaged per employee. Projected: open gaps with an approved course per employee; optimistic = all close, conservative = only 1-level gaps close in one cycle.
kpi_impact_rollup.k21_method: Proxy: % of the 55 focus-role employees meeting the requirement on all 3 primary K2.1 competencies (COMP01, COMP02, COMP07). Optimistic = every open gap with a course closes; conservative = only 1-level gaps close.
kpi_impact_rollup.insights: Without targeted paths, K2.2 runs at about half the target. Projected K2.2 is about twice the annual target, so paths should be phased over ~2 cycles. K2.1 optimistic 100% is a ceiling (no content gap in K2.1 competencies).
kpi_impact_rollup.limitations: Best-case projections. Completion is not competence: real gap closure needs reassessment, manager feedback and on-the-job evidence (Logic Model stops at Outputs, ADR-0021). K2.1 covers focus-role employees only and uses competency as a stand-in for certification. K1.1/K1.2 out of scope.
kpi_impact_rollup.phasing_refinement: Per-person phasing (ADR-0050): 8 of 55 finish in 1 cycle, 22 in 2, 25 need 3 or more.

courses.csv is built by a COURSE_SPEC-style procedural generator (150 synthetic + 4 real rows).
NB02 builds and persists both TF-IDF (production) and embedding (comparison) matchers and reuses the embeddings for duplicate detection.
A human-in-the-loop curation_status field sits between matching and path generation, and a KPI Impact Rollup traces paths back to strategic_goals/kpis.
kpi_competency_mapping covers K2.1 only; KPIs typed by lineage; K2.2 reworded to an annual cadence.
Ground-truth course labels are persisted for benchmarking only; 24 rows are NULL by design.
The classifier-vs-TF-IDF benchmark is non-discriminating on synthetic data; the generator is not changed to make it harder.
LDA topic count is chosen by coherence after data-driven filler-word removal; exploratory only.
Duplicate detection uses a 0.95 cosine threshold on MiniLM vectors with connected components; detection only.
NB02 simulates curation with a rule (methods agree and score gap < 0.10).
The 19 ld_reviewed matches were resolved by a blind side-by-side L&D review with logged reasons; no automatic next-best replacement.
Skills with no suitable course appear in paths as 'coming soon' steps with interim manager/mentor support, and are logged as content gaps.
Paths are rule-based: biggest gap first, Knowledge > Skill > Behavior, shared course once, duplicate check; ksb_layer is a fit check only.
KPI Impact Rollup is computed in NB03 with optimistic and conservative projections, aggregate only; charted in NB04.
Fixes go into generating code, not generated CSVs; employee IDs follow joining order; re-run guards protect enriched files.
The per-employee access demo shows only an employee's own path; the design is described as GDPR-aligned, not compliant.
Repo is published in full under CC BY-NC 4.0 (credit required, no commercial use), not MIT.
Long paths are phased over annual cycles with two caps (35 course hours, 6 KSBs); display only.
NB04 figures are static matplotlib PNGs in reports/figures, step-numbered, one colour-blind-safe palette, numbers read from data.
Demo paths are picked by a median rule; charts use the same privacy gate as NB03; NB04 loads no PII.
Version 2 ideas are kept in a private knowledge-base file, not in Drive or GitHub.
Notes use two layers: a plain line, then an 'Under the hood' sub-bullet; code comments carry substep numbers.
Aggregate views hide groups under MIN_GROUP_SIZE (5); fixed in reporting, never by changing the data.

path_phasing.note: Added Thread 6. NB04 Step 4.3 (ADR-0050). Display only: computed in memory, not saved, no schema change.
path_phasing.grounding: User's industry practice: 40 learning hours per year; mandatory and compliance modules assigned one at a time (max 3 a year, 45 to 60 minutes each, mostly Q3) plus QMS training, about 5 hours in total. K2.2 target gives 6 KSBs per year.
path_phasing.rule: Steps in path order; a new cycle starts when the next step would break either cap. A shared course counts as 2 KSBs. 'Coming soon' steps are pending and not placed in a cycle.
path_phasing.result: 638 path steps. Employees by cycles needed: 1 cycle 8, 2 cycles 22, 3 or more cycles 25 (shown banded, ADR-0055). KSB cap set all 73 cycle breaks; hours cap never reached (mean path 6.6 course hours; max 5.9 hours in one cycle). By role: Solution Architects avg 1.8 cycles / 4.8 course hours; ID Leads avg 2.4 cycles / 6.8 course hours.
path_phasing.insight: Absorption, not time, is the limit. Almost half of employees need 3 or more years; the NB03 'about 2 cycles' was an average. Real life: prioritise role-critical competencies first (not built). Paths are revisited every year; only Year 1 is a real plan, since a 3-year plan does not suit fast-changing skills.
path_phasing.limitations: Course minutes are seat time only; practice and on-the-job application are not captured. No grounded practice-time multiplier exists, so none is applied.

documentation_conventions.two_layer_notes: Notebook markdown leads with a plain-language line; an indented 'Under the hood' sub-bullet names the function, file or rule. README uses the plain layer only. Code comments stay technical.
documentation_conventions.substep_numbering: Every comment block in a code cell carries its substep number (Step N.x.y), from NB04 Step 4.2 onwards.
documentation_conventions.insights_style: Notes/Insights: short, everyday words; no em dashes.
